title: Tenant-Aware Audit Architecture & Migration Planning
mode: read-only source inspection and migration planning

sourceChecks.name: Operational audit schema has visible tenant field
Operational audit writer accepts explicit tenant context
Operational audit listing applies tenant filter
Financial audit schema has visible tenant field
Financial audit service shows tenant-context signal

migrationStages.name: Inventory and baseline
actions: Back up audit collections and record counts/indexes
Inventory every AuditService.record call site and financial snapshot source
Agree tenant ownership source for each source model

migrationStages.name: Schema compatibility
actions: Add optional tenantId to operational and financial audit schemas in a separate reviewed code change
Add compound indexes only after checking query patterns and duplicate/index build impact
Keep legacy entries readable while ownership remains unresolved
exitCriteria: Index plan tested against representative data

migrationStages.name: Explicit tenant context
actions: Introduce a typed audit context carrying authenticated tenantId and actor ID
Update each writer to pass validated tenant context; do not infer tenant from email
Trace financial snapshot tenantId from verified source records
exitCriteria: Missing-context behavior explicitly defined and tested

migrationStages.name: Backfill and reconciliation
actions: Backfill only records whose tenant can be deterministically established from authoritative source data
Mark ambiguous legacy records as unresolved in a controlled migration ledger; never guess
Run dry-run counts, duplicate checks, and tenant distribution reconciliation

migrationStages.name: Tenant-scoped reads and authorization
actions: Require authenticated tenant scope for list/read endpoints
Enforce role policy and tenant scope server-side, not from client-supplied tenant IDs
Add cross-tenant read/write and role-negative runtime tests
exitCriteria: Runtime tests pass in disposable environment
No unscoped audit list path remains

migrationStages.name: Controlled enforcement and release
actions: Deploy compatible schema first, then writers, then verified backfill, then scoped reads
Monitor missing-tenant events and reconciliation metrics
Only make tenant attribution required after all writers and legacy rows are reconciled

legacyDataPolicy.rule: Never infer tenant ownership from actor email or incomplete metadata.
legacyDataPolicy.knownTenant: Backfill only from an authoritative, deterministic source with reconciliation evidence.
legacyDataPolicy.unknownTenant: Leave unresolved, quarantine from tenant-scoped views, and route to an approved manual reconciliation workflow.
legacyDataPolicy.destructiveChanges: No schema field is made required and no data is changed by this planner.

limitations: Read-only static inspection; no database connection, API execution, migration, or production build was performed.
A source signal is not proof of runtime enforcement.
Call-site file inventory does not count or prove the correctness of every call path.
Migration stages are a plan requiring engineering, security, data-owner, and operational approval.
